claim: Five Account sync/composition fixture files at frozen inputs; no whole-wrapper or immutable aggregate qualification

summary.claim: Only this bounded selection; no native aggregate or release qualification.

limits: This selection integrates five complete existing files, with 7 batch, 5 scheduler control, 1 generated, 4 native control and 12 native cases. Scheduler controls are Node-only; the other four borrow an owned Chromium CDP endpoint. No product source or case identity changes. Historical git show calls gain 5000-ms/2-MiB bounds. File deadlines are 300/90/450/150/600 seconds; browser startup 15 seconds and drain grace 5 seconds. Batch adopts the prior liveness ownership group's 300-second budget as its own ceiling, not equivalence to the group. Other four bounds match account-sync/run.mjs. Original wrappers are unchanged and remain separate obligations.

The first focused scheduler run failed all five cases before assertions: the copied module could no longer resolve the runtime EnvelopeSizeError import added in R-01. The repair rewrites exactly that import to the real current protocol module with its original transitive dependencies. It does not stub or remove the class. All five baseline/mutant comparisons now pass. Copied modules live beneath ignored test-results in the disposable checkout and are removed by test cleanup.

Five virtual-clock controls compare fairness, overlap exclusion, sticky halt, observer-pressure resume and wake during active work. Four native control cases cover five omissions: final submit offline/pressure gates, retained union witness, self-stream byte binding and refusal classification. A further no-preflight omission within the native file observes forbidden reservation allocation; an unrelated thrown error cannot satisfy that assertion. Mutations require exact anchors.

Seven batch cases include six CDP renderer deaths, before/after actual IDB position-batch, attempt and envelope commits; all eight originals map to one position after reopen. The seventh loses an actual accepted submit reply, adds three later originals and compares exact retry bytes, [8,3] grouping, capture identity and additional encryption invocation count. Renderer death is not browser-process crash, power loss or a separate-profile reopen.

Eight fixed-seed histories (9112062, numRuns:8, endOnFailure:true, 420-second test bound) use the actual synthetic loopback service. Five to seven actions combine edit/offline-edit/lost-send/lost-read/compact/restart; all six types must occur. After every action text, capture count, source-to-position mapping, send/read progress, distinct request count and encryption invocation count agree. Repeated positions must retry the exact wire. Lost send aborts a fetched actual response; lost read aborts the request; offline toggles navigator.onLine plus synthetic events. Each context closes per history, while base service/connection cleanup occurs at outer test completion.

Twelve native cases include a real ciphertext service round trip, unknown submit result received before send resolution, native submission/receive aborts, shared permit drain on close, local admission during held sealing and retained signed conflict without loss of valid Local content. Five R-01 variants cover fitting/oversize/no-preflight/old sealed/old prepared-submission. The last two seed 600-KiB originals using two exact pre-R-01 Git files plus one current-code sealer mutation, then reopen under current code. They compare retained originals, stable positions/submission state and no extra seal invocation on restart. The current protocol decoder is deliberately retained; this is not a complete old app build.

Only the native file executes those historical Git paths. Its receipt pins both reference/revision/path/content hashes; the existing runner checks before launch/reuse and after execution. The owner controls exercise both new paths with real Git blob replacement while checkout identity stays unchanged, requiring prelaunch rejection, different keys after replanning and failure/drain after midrun change. The previous expected-positive service-path orphan classification remains unresolved despite subsequent passes; no fix is claimed.

The fixture chain builds in memory and registers base cleanup before setup, borrows only a validated loopback CDP endpoint, creates fresh synthetic contexts/SQLite services and drains worker and browser groups. The batch report import also loads the liveness/residue helper modules, but does not call their independent browser/service fixture constructors. Its seven JSON reports go beneath ignored test-results inside the disposable checkout; they are not retained or asserted as output obligations here. Other ACCOUNT_REPORT_DIR exports remain disabled. Original wrapper output/order/prerequisites need separate postconditions.

All 92 pure runner tests and 23 Node owner tests pass. Five Vitest-process and twelve native-owner tests retain pinned earlier evidence; their implementation/fixtures remain unchanged and were not rerun. All 174 prior general contracts / 1444 case identities and six retired-v8 exclusions remain unchanged. This selection adds bounded execution evidence, not a complete wrapper or immutable aggregate result.

The input archive retains the exact execution base, source/dependency/runtime/browser identities. Documentation/evidence written after execution does not alter the captured identity or establish an immutable aggregate. The preceding receive-driver phase was signed and verified before this run. Personal profiles/services/builds/recovery/factor material, earlier vectors/evidence/debts/signing backups and L-2 remain untouched.
